subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Enzymes speed up reactions by:
questions.explain: Enzymes provide a lower-energy pathway without changing the equilibrium.

questions.q: The part of an enzyme where the substrate binds is the:
questions.explain: The active site is complementary in shape and chemistry to the substrate.

questions.q: Heating an enzyme above its optimum decreases activity because it:
options: Denatures the enzyme, changing the active site
questions.explain: Excess heat disrupts tertiary structure so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: A competitive inhibitor reduces activity by:
options: Binding the active site and blocking the substrate
questions.explain: Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate; their effect can be overcome by more substrate.

questions.q: Reactions that build large molecules from small ones, using energy, are:
questions.explain: Anabolism builds up; catabolism breaks down.

questions.q: The universal short-term energy currency of cells is:
questions.explain: ATP releases energy when its terminal phosphate is hydrolysed.

questions.q: In eukaryotes, glycolysis occurs in the:
questions.explain: Glycolysis splits glucose into two pyruvate in the cytoplasm without oxygen.

questions.q: In aerobic respiration, the final electron acceptor is:
questions.explain: Oxygen accepts electrons and forms water; without it the chain stops.

questions.q: In human muscle during intense exercise, anaerobic respiration produces:
questions.explain: Humans make lactate; yeast make ethanol and CO2.

questions.q: Aerobic respiration yields far more ATP per glucose than anaerobic respiration because:
options: Oxygen and the electron transport chain allow much more ATP to be made
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration (~30–38 ATP) far exceeds the 2 net ATP of anaerobic glycolysis.

questions.q: The light-dependent reactions occur in the:
questions.explain: The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma; light reactions in the thylakoids.

questions.q: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from:
questions.explain: Water is split into electrons, protons and oxygen in the light-dependent reactions.

questions.q: The light-independent (Calvin) cycle fixes:
questions.explain: CO2 is fixed using ATP and NADPH to form carbohydrate.

questions.q: When light is plentiful, the rate of photosynthesis often plateaus because it is limited by:
options: Another factor such as CO2 or temperature
questions.explain: At the plateau a different factor becomes limiting.

questions.q: Chlorophyll appears green because it:
options: Absorbs red and blue light and reflects green
questions.explain: Its absorption spectrum matches the action spectrum of photosynthesis.

questions.q: The induced-fit model states that on binding, the active site:
options: Changes shape slightly to fit the substrate
questions.explain: Binding causes a conformational change that aids catalysis.

questions.q: When all active sites are occupied at high substrate concentration, the rate:
questions.explain: At saturation the enzymes are the limiting factor.

questions.q: The Krebs cycle takes place in the:
questions.explain: The link reaction and Krebs cycle occur in the matrix.

questions.q: ATP and NADPH from the light reactions are used in the Calvin cycle to:
questions.explain: They provide energy and reducing power to fix CO2.

questions.q: Metabolism is best described as:
options: The sum of all enzyme-controlled reactions in an organism
questions.explain: It includes both anabolic and catabolic pathways.
